summary: An Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Waseda University, Ikuhisa Takigawa served as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Waseda University and Tokai University, attested in 2002.

Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Ikuko Tazaki held posts attested in 2017 as a special researcher at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute and as a collaborative researcher at Kyoto University.

A religious studies scholar, Ilkka Pyysiäinen completed a PhD at the University of Helsinki (attested 1993) under René Gothóni. He served as an Academy Research Fellow at Helsinki in 1984 and as a visiting researcher at Oxford.

A sinologist and tibetologist, Galambos studied at Eötvös Loránd University, Nankai University, and UC Berkeley (PhD, 2002). He worked at the British Library (2002–2012), University of Cambridge (2012–2023), and Zhejiang University (~2023).

Imre Hamar studied at Eötvös Loránd University and National Taiwan Normal University, and under Noritoshi Aramaki (~1995–1996). He was a visiting professor at Otani University (~2002–2003) and became a professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006.

A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, In-gun Kang studied at the Jesuit School of Theology, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Heythrop College, earning a doctoral degree supervised by Michael Barnes.

Working in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Ines Konczak-Nagel held posts as a postdoctoral research fellow at Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University in 2012.
A scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies, Ingmar Heise earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University by 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, Ingo Strauch earned his PhD from Free University of Berlin by 2000 and held a post there (attested 2008). He was attested as a professor at the University of Lausanne in 2018.
Inyoung Chung is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2008) under the supervision of Paul Groner.

A scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology, Culianu studied at Bucharest, Catholic University of the Sacred Heart, and Paris-Sorbonne, and under Mircea Eliade. He held posts at the University of Groningen (1976–1986) and Chicago Divinity School (1986–1991).

An Indology and history/archaeology scholar, Irawati Karve studied at Fergusson College, Huzurpaga, and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (~1926–1928). She later held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~1959–1960).

A historian and Indologist, Irfan Habib studied at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University (~1949–1953), and New College (~1953–1958). He served as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from ~1953 to 1991.

Irving Babbitt, working in philosophy, studied at Harvard College, the University of Paris, and Harvard University. He held academic posts at Williams College (~1893–1894) and Harvard University (~1894–1933).

A scholar of history and archaeology, Isaac Schapera studied at Cándido Candi, the University of Cape Town, and the London School of Economics. He later held posts at the London School of Economics (~1950–1969), Toronto, and Chicago.

Specializing in Tibetology, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies, Schmidt earned a doctorate at Rostock (~1826). He served at the Russian Bible Society (~1814–1824) and held a professorship at the University of Saint Petersburg (~1833–1847).

A Tibetology scholar, Henrion-Dourcy studied at the Free University of Brussels, Harvard, EPHE, and Tibet University, with teachers Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She held posts teaching anthropology at Laval University (~2004, 2007).

Isabelle Onians is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed a PhD at the University of Oxford by 2002. Attested in 2007, she served as an editor for the Clay Sanskrit Library.

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Ratié studied at Paris 1 and EPHE under Lyne Bansat-Boudon and Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at Leipzig, Sorbonne Nouvelle University (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).
A philosopher educated at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1928–1932), Isaiah Berlin held an academic post at the University of Oxford from ~1932 to 1997.
